quarterly_data.quarter: Novo Nordisk press release: Novo Nordisk STEP Young phase 3 data: 40.4% of children (09-07-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: First results from the STEP Young phase 3 trial of once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide (with reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity) in 165 children aged 6 to under 12 years with obesity: the trial met its primary endpoint, showing superior BMI reduction versus placebo at week 68; 40.4% of children treated with semaglutide were no longer classified as having obesity after 68 weeks versus none (0%) on placebo (trial product estimand), although more than 85% had class II or III severe obesity at baseline. Safety and tolerability were consistent with adult and adolescent semaglutide trials, with no new safety concerns and none for growth or pubertal development. The trial is run under regulatory post-marketing requirements for the semaglutide phase 3 programme.
quarterly_data.figure: 40.4% no longer classified as having obesity vs 0% placebo at week 68; 165 children aged 6 to under 12; more than 85% class II or III at baseline
